```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

memdash is a Shiny dashboard for [Memgraph](https://memgraph.com). It connects
over **Bolt** using the official Python `neo4j` driver through **reticulate**,
so plain openCypher works unmodified.

## 1. Prerequisites

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Python driver in the reticulate Python environment
reticulate::py_install("neo4j")

# Install this package
devtools::install("r-package/memdash")
```

Start Memgraph, e.g.:

```bash
docker run -p 7687:7687 memgraph/memgraph
```

## 2. Launch the dashboard

```{r, eval = FALSE}
memdash::run_memdash()
```

In the app: set **Bolt URI** to `bolt://localhost:7687`, press **Connect**,
then **Load demo data** and **Run all**. For Memgraph Enterprise
multi-tenancy, set **Tenant database** (default `stxp4rd`).

## 3. Use it in code

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(memdash)

memgraph_connect("bolt://localhost:7687", database = "stxp4rd")  # tenant DB
memdash_seed_demo()

# Metric
res <- memgraph_query("MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes")
records_to_df(res$records, res$fields)

# Graph card data
res <- memgraph_query("MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN n, r, m LIMIT 50")
g <- records_to_graph(res$records)
length(g$nodes)  # visNetwork-ready nodes
length(g$edges)  # visNetwork-ready edges

# igraph / tidygraph layouts for graph cards
ig <- records_to_igraph(res$records)
coords <- igraph_layout_coords(ig, "kk")     # n x 2 fixed coordinates
ggraph_from_records(res$records, "fr")       # static ggplot
# In the app: set a graph card's layout to "kk", "drl", ..., or "ggraph"
new_card(type = "graph", layout = "kk",
         cypher = "MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN n, r, m LIMIT 100")

# Parameters ($limit is substituted as a quoted literal)
memgraph_query("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name LIMIT $limit",
               params = list(limit = "10"))

memgraph_disconnect()
```

## 4. Build, save and share dashboards

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Editable builder: add/edit/delete cards, per-card Run and auto-refresh
run_memdash()

# Cards are plain lists — build your own
cards <- default_cards()
cards[[1]] <- new_card(title = "People", type = "table",
                       cypher = "MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.name AS name, p.born AS born")

# Persist as portable JSON (same schema as the web app)
save_dashboard(cards, "my_dashboard.json")

# Anyone with the package can recreate the dashboard
d <- load_dashboard("my_dashboard.json")
memdash_app(cards = d$cards)               # editable copy
memdash_app(dashboard_file = "my_dashboard.json")  # read-only viewer
run_memdash(read_only = TRUE)               # read-only mode for current cards
```

\code{read_only = TRUE} hides all editing controls so a second user can view and
run the dashboard without being able to change it. It is an app-level flag —
the JSON file itself is plain text; for real access control, keep the canonical
file somewhere the viewer cannot write.
